cards.question: Tell me about yourself.
cards.hint: Present, past, future: what you do now, one or two proof points that got you here, and why this role is the next step. Keep it under two minutes.
cards.example: I'm a software engineer with five years of experience building digital products, mostly at startups. For the last two years I've been a full-stack developer at a fintech, where I helped launch two versions of a payments platform that grew from 5,000 to 50,000 users in six months. I owned our APIs and front-end performance, working in an agile team to ship fast without losing quality. Now I'm looking for a place where I can keep building products that scale, and that's what caught my attention here.

cards.question: Walk me through your resume.
cards.hint: Tell it as a story with a thread. One sentence per step, more detail on the most recent and relevant role.

cards.question: Give me a quick overview of your background.
cards.hint: The 60-second version of "tell me about yourself": current role, main strength, why you are here.

cards.question: How would you describe your career so far?
cards.hint: Name the thread that connects your jobs (a skill, a domain, a type of problem) and where it is taking you.

cards.question: What do you do in your current role?
cards.hint: Scope, team and impact: what you own, who you work with and one result you are proud of.

cards.question: Tell me something about you that is not on your resume.
cards.hint: Pick something human that still says something about how you work: a hobby, a side project, a habit.

cards.question: How did you get into this field?
cards.hint: A short origin story, then connect it to what still motivates you today.

cards.question: Why do you want to work here?
cards.hint: Connect something specific about the company (mission, product, market) to something specific about you. Avoid generic praise, and never lead with salary or benefits.
cards.example: I really admire how you're using AI to make financial services accessible to more people. I worked at a SaaS startup before and saw how technology can change a whole market. My experience with scalable architecture would be useful at this stage of fast growth, and I'd love to be part of a team that's leading innovation in finance.

cards.question: Why are you looking for a new role?
cards.hint: Stay positive and forward-looking: what you want to grow into, not what you are running from.

cards.question: Why are you interested in this position?
cards.hint: Link two or three requirements of the role to your experience, then say what excites you about it.
cards.example: What interested me most is the chance to work on automation and innovation projects, which I have experience in and really enjoy. My background at startups prepared me for fast-changing environments and creative problem solving. I'm excited about using those skills to help the team reach its goals.

cards.question: What do you know about our company?
cards.hint: Show you did your homework: product, customers, a recent change. Then one sentence on why it matters to you.
cards.example: I know you're leading the edtech space with your adaptive learning platform, and I saw you recently raised a Series B to expand internationally. I like how you combine AI with personalized education, and with my machine learning background I think I could help improve your content recommendations.

cards.question: Why do you want to work for an international company?
cards.hint: Talk about the work, the team and what you will learn. Money can be part of it, but don't lead with it.

cards.question: Why did you leave your previous job?
cards.hint: Frame it as moving toward something: new challenges and growth. Never criticize your last employer, and don't make salary the only reason.
cards.example: I left to take on bigger challenges and grow as a full-stack developer. I learned a lot about backend systems there, but I felt it was time for a faster, more product-driven environment. I'm excited to join an agile team where I can use what I know, learn new technologies and help scale a product that's growing quickly.

cards.question: What attracted you to this job description?
cards.hint: Quote one or two concrete items from the posting and explain why they match what you want next.

cards.question: Have you used our product?
cards.hint: If yes, share one thing you like and one idea. If no, say what you learned about it and what you would try first.

cards.question: What are you looking for in your next role?
cards.hint: Name two or three concrete things (scope, team, problems) and tie them to this role.

cards.question: Where do you see yourself in five years?
cards.hint: Show ambition that fits the company: the skills and scope you want to grow into, not a job title.
cards.example: In five years I see myself as a senior engineer or tech lead, leading a team on challenging projects. I'm very interested in learning more about scalability and leading agile teams, which I think this role offers given how fast you're growing. I'd love to help build products that take the company global, and grow together with the team.

cards.question: What do you value most in a job?
cards.hint: Pick one value and give a short example of a time it made a difference for you.
cards.example: What I value most are learning opportunities and a collaborative environment. I like places where I face challenges that help me grow and where ideas are shared to find the best solutions. That's what creates real impact, and I see it as part of your culture.

cards.question: What kind of team do you work best in?
cards.hint: Describe the environment and give an example. Show you can adapt to other styles too.

cards.question: What are you most proud of in your career so far?
cards.hint: One achievement with context, your part and the result. Save the details for follow-up questions.

cards.question: Have you worked remotely before?
cards.hint: Show the habits that make remote work: async communication, clear updates, managing your own time.

cards.question: Have you worked with people from other countries?
cards.hint: Give a concrete example: time zones, cultural differences you noticed, and how you adapted.

cards.question: How comfortable are you communicating in English at work?
cards.hint: Be confident and honest. Mention where you use English today (meetings, docs, clients).

cards.question: What would your current manager say about you?
cards.hint: Two or three traits, each with a quick example. If possible, quote real feedback you received.

cards.question: Why should we hire you?
cards.hint: Summarize the match: their top needs, your matching proof points, and what you would bring in the first months.

cards.question: What do you hope to learn in this role?
cards.hint: Name something specific that matters for the role, and show how learning it also benefits the company.
cards.example: I hope to learn more about integrating systems at large scale and optimizing processes to scale products. That would complement my full-stack experience and let me contribute even more to your projects. I'm excited to bring my skills to the team and grow with the company.
